messages.subject: "inconsistent dimensionality": vector with 1 element
parts:
Dear Nimble people,

I have a nimbleCode that contains the following line:

code <- nimble::nimbleCode({
...
for(v in 1:Cn){
somevariate[v] ~ dnorm(mean=Cmean1[v], var=Cvarm1[v])
}
...
})

The constant "Cn" is declared in a list of constants before the code.

This code is meant to have a general application, and "Cn" is the number of variates of a given type that appear in a specific application. Its value is set in the list of constants before the code. Also the value of "Cmean1" is set in the constants, as

Cmean1 = rep(0, Cn)


In cases with Cn>1, everything works fine. However, in cases with Cn=1 I get the following error when calling nimbleModel():

Error in addMissingIndexingRecurse(code[[i]], dimensionsList) :
inconsistent dimensionality provided for node 'Cmean1'

My hypothesis is that this happens because Nimble sees Cmean1 declared as a scalar, but it interprets is as a vector within the code.

Two questions:

• Until some months ago I did not experience this problem, even when Cn=1. At that time I was declaring "Cmean1" in the inits function, same way as above. So now I've tried moving its declaration from the constants to the inits, but the problem described above remains. Maybe something has changed in more recent versions of Nimble?

• Any suggestions on how to bypass this problem and keeping the generality of the code? I've tried using setSize or explicitly declaring the dimension within nimbleModel(), as described in the manual; but the problem remains.

I know that in this simple example I could replace "mean=Cmean1[v]" with "mean=0" in the code. However, I would like to keep the possibility of assigning different values for Cmean1 in cases with Cn>1.

Cheers!
Luca

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: "inconsistent dimensionality": vector with 1 element
parts:
Luca, thanks for the question, and our usual apologies about the annoyance distinguishing between true scalars versus length-1-vectors, as often arise in nimbleModels, and also in private data elements of nimbleFunctions.

For now, although not ideal, you can use the if(...) syntax inside the model code.  This will conditionally declare (or not declare) lines of code, depending on the evaluation of the if(...) condition.  So (I believe) you can work around your problem as:

code <- nimbleCode({
    for(i in 1:N) {
        if(N == 1) x_mean[i] <- mu
        if(N  > 1) x_mean[i] <- mu[i]
        x[i] ~ dnorm(x_mean[i], 1)
    }
})

N <- 1    ## either is ok
N <- 2    ## either is ok
constants <- list(N = N, mu = rep(0,N))
data <- list(x = rep(0,N))
inits <- list()

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)

As a separate aside, maybe I was doing something wrong, but the problem you described went away for me when I moved "mu" out of the constants list, and instead into the initial values list.  But maybe this is due to a recent fix/change, since I'm using a pre-release version of the package.  Regardless, the code above should (I hope) get you going.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: "inconsistent dimensionality": vector with 1 element
parts:
Yes Luca, your observations are exactly correct: "constant" values cannot be modified, as specifying something as a "constant" has the effect to "baked in" the numeric value to the model - these no longer represent mutable model variables, but instead hard-coded numbers in the model internals.  This results in an overall smaller model structure, fewer nodes, a smaller graph structure, faster compilation, etc.

Now if only my cookies came out as well.

Cheers,
Daniel
